correctness.rationale: Each original maximal constant run is fully specified for both track words by one integer x_i; any allocation is realizable by a position coloring. The 3-state partition fixes output run signatures. Matching signatures give exact run-length equations; each free x_i appears in exactly two degree incidences, possibly both at one vertex (loop). Thus feasible allocations are equivalent to exact-degree capacitated b-matchings. Polynomial-time general capacitated b-matching with binary capacities gives 3^r poly(r,S). verify.py independently corroborates reduction for 5327 binary/ternary words and a 117-bit compressed positive example. The infinite proof does not rest on enumeration; the classical matching solver is an explicit external premise.

value.rationale: Unrestricted binary shuffle-square recognition is NP-complete (Bulteau–Vialette 2020). The result provides a deterministic single-exponential algorithm in the natural and compressible number of runs, using O(r) graph vertices/edges and bit-cost polynomial in run lengths. This is a genuine structural tractability theorem across arbitrary finite alphabets and enormous compressed inputs, not a routine finite census or alphabet renaming.
